title: `get_playback_position()` in HTML5 freezes/gets delayed about one second when playing a sound
body:
### Tested versions

- This issue was originally found on Godot v4.6.stable.steam [89cea1439], but it can be reproducible from version v4.5.beta7.official [4ebf67c12] onwards, where issue #109790 was resolved, relating to `get_playback_position()` on web.
- This bug isn't present on versions previous to v4.5.beta1.official [46c495ca2], however in this version `get_playback_position()` is updated much less frequently (issue #105397).
- The desired result can be seen on version v4.5.beta2.official [e1b4101e3], the one that included the pull which included the resolved #105397 issue: the bug isn't present and `get_playback_position()` is updated frequently/correctly.

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable (89cea1439) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21924.61) - AMD Ryzen 5 PRO 4650G with Radeon Graphics (12 threads) - 15.37 GiB memory

### Issue description

When calling the `play()` function on a AudioStreamPlayer, the `get_playback_position()` function always gets stuck at value `0.00266666663811` (this value may vary depending on hardware) for about one second and then restarts, now working properly, but having a second delay with the audio. This **causes `get_playback_position()` to not represent the actual playback position of the current playing audio.**

This only happens when the game is ran on HTML5. Android and Windows builds don't have this issue.

A workaround for this is to measure the delay by comparing `Time.get_ticks_usec()` when playing the audio and when `get_playback_position()` passes the `0.00266666663811` value, and then adding the delay to the value that `get_playback_position()` returns to get the real playback.

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout
	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
	AudioBPM.play()
	time1 = Time.get_ticks_usec()

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	print(AudioBPM.get_playback_position())

	if not calculated and AudioBPM.get_playback_position() > 0.00266666663811:
		time2 = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		delay = (time2 - time1) / 1000000.0
		print("DELAY: " + str(delay))
		calculated = true

	var real_playback = AudioBPM.get_playback_position() + delay
```
However, this still makes the real value of the audio's playback inaccessible in this second.

This video shows the desired result of `get_playback_position()`, in a HTML5 build made in v4.5.beta2.official [e1b4101e3]. The moving bar represents the playback position of the song. Ignore the bar's highlighting.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/675edc52-981d-44a1-9384-34e456618c32

This video shows the bug explained in this issue, in a HTML5 build made in v4.6.stable.steam [89cea1439]:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fca57427-a4b7-4123-8bc0-9f94ab0a2f7c

(The music used for the videos is called Sburban Jungle and I do not own it. It was just used for testing :-))

### Steps to reproduce

Run the Minimal reproduction project on version v4.5.beta7.official [4ebf67c12] or later of Godot and install the Build Template for HTML5. Run the project in your browser using Remote Deploy. You can open DevTools to see the values of the audio's `get_playback_position()`.

Notice how the audio plays in the background, but the bar stays still for a second, indicated by the "DELAY" text. If you run the project on version v4.5.beta2.official [e1b4101e3], this won't happen.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-get-playback-position-issueV2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25188487/mrp-get-playback-position-issueV2.zip)
